title: Etale proper-support normalization intertwines exchange and projection
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $e:V\to T$ be a separated etale morphism of finite type between Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and choose a compactification $c=(j:V\hookrightarrow\overline V,r:\overline V\to T)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Work on the small etale sites in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with exact inverse image $a^*=a^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Put $F_e^c=Rr_*Dj_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and $S_e=D(e_{\Sigma!})$, where $e_{\Sigma!}$ is exact sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Let $c_e^c:F_e^c\xrightarrow{\sim}S_e$ be the canonical proper-support comparison of [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], using its identification of proper-support sections with sum extension.

The inverse of $c_e^c$ has the following normalization. On a sheaf $M$, the map on presheaf summands before sheafification inducing its degree-zero map $e_{\Sigma!}M\to r_*j_!M$ sends a summand indexed by a lift $s:W\to V$ over an etale test object $W\to T$ to the section with the given value on the graph of $s$ in $\overline V\times_TW$ and zero on its complement; this specifies the induced sheaf morphism, rather than identifying sheaf sections objectwise with the presheaf direct sum. On complexes it is this degreewise sheaf identification followed by the derived-functor comparison $D(r_*j_!)\to Rr_*Dj_!$. It intertwines the following specified transformations.

(1) Let $g:T'\to T$ be any morphism with $T'$ Noetherian, let $V'=V\times_TT'$ have projections $e':V'\to T'$ and $h:V'\to V$, and use the pulled-back compactification $c'=(j',r')$, with $\bar h:\overline V\times_TT'\to\overline V$. Let $b_j:\bar h^*Dj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Dj'_!h^*$ and $b_e:g^*S_e\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{e'}h^*$ be the degreewise inverses of the specified sum-extension comparison [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map, lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], for $j$ and $e$, respectively. Define $C^c_{e,g}=Rr'_*(b_j)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{r}$ using the proper direct-image exchange, namely the adjunction mate of the pullback-composition identification [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Then
$$ (c_{e'}^{c'}h^*)\circ C^c_{e,g}=b_e\circ(g^*c_e^c). $$

(2) For $M\in D(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ let $\pi_{r,Dj_!M,K}$ be the ordinary-etale counit-defined projection map [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Let $\gamma_{j,M,r^*K}:Dj_!M\otimes_A^L r^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Dj_!(M\otimes_A^L e^*K)$ be the canonical open-extension tensor comparison [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor], inserting $j^*r^*=e^*$. Put
$$ P^c_{e,M,K}=Rr_*(\gamma_{j,M,r^*K})\circ\pi_{r,Dj_!M,K}. $$
Let $p^\Sigma_{e,M,K}:S_eM\otimes_A^LK\xrightarrow{\sim}S_e(M\otimes_A^Le^*K)$ be the derived sum-extension projection isomorphism: on tensor representatives its sheaf map sends $(s,m)\otimes k$ to $(s,m\otimes s^*k)$ on the same lift $s:W\to V$. Then
$$ c_e^c(M\otimes_A^Le^*K)\circ P^c_{e,M,K}=p^\Sigma_{e,M,K}\circ(c_e^c(M)\otimes1_K). $$
Both identities are identities of derived natural transformations. They hold for every chosen compactification $c$, including those for which $r$ is not finite, and agree with the proper-refinement identifications.

source.place: Tags 0F4Y (lemma-separated-etale-shriek), 0GKM (lemma-Rf-shriek-for-quasi-finite), 0F7L (lemma-base-change-shriek), 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), 0GL5 (lemma-projection-formula-Rf-lower-shriek); etale-cohomology.tex Tags 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), 0F4L (lemma-shriek-into-star-separated-etale, graph-section construction). Agent formulation of compatibility of the canonical proper-support comparison with the specified derived maps, not a verbatim single Stacks lemma.

proof.text: Choose an EtaleCompactSupportNormalization N from its nonemptiness theorem. Use N.sheafComparison and N.comparison for the two families. The sheaf and homotopy normalization equations and the arbitrary-base-change equation are precisely fields of N.

For each sheaf M apply degree-zero homology to N.derived_normalization on the single complex M. The total right-derived unit of the left-exact proper direct-image functor is an isomorphism in degree zero. Naturality transports this along the canonical open-extension/single-complex isomorphism. Cancel the remaining isomorphisms in the homotopy formula. The single-complex homology comparison identifies the resulting isomorphism with the sheafComparison component itself. Componentwise invertibility proves the sheaf natural transformation invertible.

Transport the monoidal structure on left-derived inverse image to exact derived inverse image. The source-library projection theorem makes its left projection mate invertible: this property is invariant under transport, since it is equivalent to invertibility of the internal-hom comparison. Braiding changes the left projection mate to the right projection mate specified in the statement. The transported tensorator is exactly etaleSupportExactUpperTensorIso. Thus the inverse of asIso of etaleSupportSumProjectionReverse supplies p, with the required inverse equation.

Transpose the inverse comparison under proper inverse image/direct image. The graph tensor evaluation theorem supplies the equality after precomposing with the sum tensor mate. Naturality of the pullback tensor comparison and the counit formula for the right-adjoint projection map identify this with the transpose of the compactification projection composite. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives the untransposed equality. Cancel the invertible reverse sum projection and the inverse normalization comparison to obtain the required projection equation.

The refinement field of N uses its inverse comparison for the coarser open immersion. Substitute the unbounded refinement-normalization theorem to identify this composite with the inverse pairwise compactification comparison. The cocycle and identity laws make the pairwise comparisons inverse to each other. Cancel them to obtain exactly the stated orientation of the refinement equation.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0GKF and 0GL5; stage 3 reuses the simultaneous graph normalization, the source derived etale projection formula, H0 of the right-derived unit, and the unbounded compactification comparisons. Only the graph tensor evaluation is a separate geometric obligation.
